title: What Forest Cities Is
definition: Forest Cities: cities where buildings and old-growth forest interleave.
description:
Forest Cities — Signature Edition: cities where buildings and old-growth forest interleave. This is the JAH-original vision, designed from first principles and labeled as Signature speculation throughout.

The Signature forest hulls program starts where public roadmaps stop. Where public research asks what is fundable, the Signature line asks what is buildable: grove districts rethought, trail transit rebuilt, canopy corridors reimagined for the century ahead. Nothing here is presented as established fact — it is a designed future, fully specified.

This edition mirrors the public database record for record — concept, components, milestones, demos, drills, alliance, roadmap — but every entry is the Signature take: bolder timelines, integrated systems thinking, and the timber blocks ambition that defines the Signature line.

title: The Signature Vision: Forest Cities
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Forest Cities.
description:
The Signature vision of Forest Cities does not ask what committees will fund — it asks what physics allows and what engineering can compound.

Signature forest hulls program, charter one: master grove districts at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale trail transit manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate canopy corridors systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Forest Cities becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

title: The forest hulls Grid
definition: The forest hulls Grid: a load-bearing component of Forest Cities.
description:
The urban backbone: power, water, data and logistics woven into one grove districts grid that the forest hulls district runs on.

In the Forest Cities architecture, the forest hulls grid is load-bearing: without it the forest hulls fails outright — Forest Cities stops being Forest Cities at all. Builders sequence this piece early because every other component assumes it works. In the Signature architecture this piece is designed first-class, not bolted on.

Maturity varies: some deployments of this piece exist today in simpler forms, while the full Forest Cities-grade version remains a research target. The readiness estimator in this database scores it honestly.

t: 2030 — The first forest hulls district opens at 50
title: 2030 — The first forest hulls district opens at 50
definition: 2030 milestone on the Forest Cities roadmap.
description:
The first forest hulls district opens at 50,000 residents, its grove districts grid and trail transit mobility running at full design load.

What must be true first: the grove districts results have to replicate outside the lab, trail transit manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and canopy corridors operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed grove districts demonstrations, trail transit cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting canopy corridors uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)
key_points: Target year: 2030 (4 years out).
Depends on: grove districts, trail transit, canopy corridors.

title: Readiness Estimator: Forest Cities
definition: Estimates Forest Cities readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Forest Cities components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a forest hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Forest Cities Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Forest Cities operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Forest Cities installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 67767 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where grove districts monitoring, trail transit redundancy, or canopy corridors maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Forest Cities Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Forest Cities: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Forest Cities — cities where buildings and old-growth forest interleave.

Phase 1 — Prove (grove districts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (trail transit): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (canopy corridors): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (timber blocks): forest hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and woodland-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
key_points: Four phases: Prove, Build, Operate, Compound.
Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
